target_customer: Enterprises and startups that outsource software builds
problem: Businesses struggled to hire and manage developers, designers and managers for custom software projects.
business_model: managed project marketplace with fixed price software builds

founders.name: Roger Dickey
founders.background_notes: Left the CEO role in 2019 to start Untitled Labs

competitors.name: Elance and oDesk (merged into Upwork)
competitors.what: Freelance marketplaces named by TechCrunch as Elance (now Upwork) and oDesk

competitors.name: Pivotal Labs
competitors.what: Agency style software consultancy aimed at enterprises and later stage startups

technical_complexity.rationale: A matching and project management platform with team workflows; difficulty was delivery quality and operations, not novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Talent was drawn from open labor markets and delivery quality depended on people, so copying was feasible.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it directly; Gigster itself later sold in a distressed deal.

market_need_then: Demand for outsourced custom software among startups and enterprises, shown by early traction and an a16z led 10 million dollar Series A five months after the batch.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand was found. The name is easily confused with Giggster, a different company, in search results.

outcome_analysis: Gigster raised about 32.5 million dollars by August 2017 from a16z and Redpoint, then the CEO left in 2019 and in May 2021 the company sold to Ionic Partners, whose later release described operational and balance sheet issues at the time. Ionic then sold it to Virtasant in March 2024. The cause of the decline is not public in detail; the model likely struggled to deliver margins on custom projects, but no source states this.
notes: Total raised of 32.5M (Wikipedia, Aug 2017) versus 35.9M (CB Insights). A 2.5M seed in July 2015 appears only on a dead startups site and is unverified. Exit chain: Ionic Partners May 2021, then Virtasant 26 March 2024; the record lists the first. No layoffs reported in sources found. Post mortem cause not public. 2015-07 seed of $2.5M now verified in the TechCrunch launch article (the earlier note saying only a dead startups site had it is superseded). Series B lead Redpoint per Wikipedia (2017-08-29). Toptal, Crew, IBM and Infosys are also named in the 2015 article as alternatives.
